messages:
maria: quick q — our async python client seems to ignore Retry-After on 429s when streaming. noticed in prod canary, requests just retry immediately and we spike.
jon: do you have a minimal repro or logs? are you using the streaming iterator or consuming .text()?
maria: streaming. example log snippet:
```
2026-03-20T14:12:34Z ERROR request_handler.py: retrying after 429, headers={\n  'Retry-After': '5',\n  'X-RateLimit-Limit': '1000',\n  'X-RateLimit-Remaining': '0',\n  'X-RateLimit-Reset': '1712000000'\n}
```
kevin: hmm. we recently changed header normalization to lowercase keys which is fine, but the streaming code path reads retry-after from response.headers.get('retry-after') and then does `int(value)` without handling HTTP-date form.
andrea: there are two formats for Retry-After: delta-seconds and HTTP-date. +1 to handling both.
maria: i can do a quick fix to parse http-date, but also noticed our client treats Retry-After as float in some places and int in others which makes typing awkward.
kevin: suggestion: add a small helper in clients/retry_utils.py:
```
async def parse_retry_after(headers: Mapping[str, str]) -> Optional[float]:
    v = headers.get('retry-after') or headers.get('Retry-After')
    if not v:
        return None
    # delta-seconds
    if v.isdigit():
        return float(v)
    # try HTTP-date
    try:
        ts = email.utils.parsedate_to_datetime(v)
        return max((ts - datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)).total_seconds(), 0.0)
    except Exception:
        return None
```
kevin: then feed that into our backoff logic (asyncio.sleep(retry_after)). Keep it typed: -> Optional[float]
jon: for the typing bit, we should export a RetryInfo TypedDict or dataclass so callers can introspect (retry_after, source_header, raw_value). avoids relying on random None/float conventions.
andrea: also +1 to adding an on_rate_limit callback hook on the client API so apps can emit metrics or do token-bucket adjustments. small API surface:
```
client = AsyncClient(..., on_rate_limit=lambda info: metrics.increment('client.rate_limited'))
```
maria: love that. would let us surface a metric and avoid silent retries. we can also expose the parsed headers (x-quota-remaining/x-quota-reset) in that payload.
kevin: note for streaming: some servers send the 429 on a chunked resp after the body starts; ensure we read response.headers early (aiohttp exposes headers before content). our current streaming wrapper delays header handling until iterating first chunk which is fine but the retry logic is in the high-level request() path. small race there.
jon: can we add unit tests that stub aiohttp and return various retry-after formats and chunked 429s? CI test should run very fast.
ci-bot: Build passed for branch fix/retry-parse (PR #4321) — tests added: tests/test_retry_headers.py
andrea: nit: document behavior in api.md — whether we treat Retry-After as advisory and max cap (e.g., cap to 60s) so app-level retry policies don't hang forever.
maria: actionable: kevin will open the PR to add parse_retry_after + typing + on_rate_limit hook. andrea will add docs note. jon will add unit tests and a small integration test for streaming 429s.
kevin: i'll also add a small change log entry and mark as non-breaking (backwards compatible) since default client behavior remains same if header absent.
maria: awesome — thanks all. will watch canary and report.
jon: feel free to @me if you want a quick review.
kevin: merging tomorrow if green. :thumbsup:
